layers.note: A low, woolly herb of late-snow meadows and alpine turf, in small patches.

moisture.note: Moist ground that dries after snowmelt.

heat_load.note: Cool aspects and snowbed hollows more than hot slopes.

elevation_m.note: Upper subalpine to alpine; about 1,500 m and up in Washington, so Paradise is near its lower edge.

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about −20 to 1 °C; gone below −30 °C and above 5 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −42 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −50 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 5 to 14 °C; gone below 3 °C, where summers are too short, and above 17 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 500 to 2,400 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 250.

degree_days_5.note: About 100 to 1,200 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 30.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.45, gone by 0.3.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit: summer-dry Cascade summers suit it; up to about 0.6 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone by 0.8.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (Paradise, about 1,650 m) from general knowledge of the species; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Woolly pussytoes grows from British Columbia and Alberta to Oregon, Idaho, Montana and Wyoming, in subalpine and alpine meadows (the PLANTS Database). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
